title: Grateful Dead Live at Unknown on 1967-02-12

ai_review.summary: A raw 1967 soundboard captures a blistering Smokestack Lightning → King Bee set, highlighted by Pigpen’s harp fury and sweet early Jerry guitar tones.
ai_review.review: Despite mixed opinions on the tape's fidelity—some note over‑saturation and digital artifacts—the recording delivers a powerful blues performance that many fans regard as a highlight of the era. Pigpen dominates with his harp and vocals while Jerry’s guitar is described as “sweet,” making the two‑song stretch a must‑listen for Deadheads.

ai_rating.rationale: The majority of reviews (over 70%) are highly positive about the performance and accept the modest recording flaws; weighting show quality heavily yields a strong overall rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crowd noise audible, some reviewers report over‑saturation, digital distortion or modulation artifacts, but many praise the tape as impressive for 1967 and better than typical audience tapes.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A concise two‑song blues jam that flows tightly, with Pigpen’s harp and vocals driving the energy and Jerry’s guitar providing sweet early‑Dead tones.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for a sweet, early‑era guitar tone; noted as “sweet as sweet can be.”
band_member_comments.Bob: Brief mention of Bob’s rhythm work at the five‑minute mark.
